figures.title: A source edit reaches one dependency step
figures.question: What changed in the observed diamond, and where does revision invalidation stop?
figures.caption: Observed isolated fixture, run-596ee23ce4f9498a, using public identity and propagation APIs. Blue arrows read claim requires premise. Orange arrows run in the opposite direction and show the observed source-identity effect: editing line 2 of A's source changes A, B and C revisions, although the selected line-1 excerpt is unchanged. D's local content revision remains unchanged. No automatic arbitrary-depth propagation is established. The companion formal-target probe run-e96422486f524d69 additionally found unchanged B/C formal target handles. The formal-target disagreement is a reproducible defect. Whether other consumers require transitive invalidation remains an open policy decision. Neither observation says that the mathematics is false.
